stem: A driver’s “safe speed” is the speed at which he can just brake to a halt in 30 m. On a dry road his safe speed is 20 m/s. It starts to snow and the coefficient of friction drops to half its dry value. What is his safe speed now (m/s, nearest integer)? (Neglect reaction time.)

A cart of mass M has a block of mass ‘m’ attached to it as shown in the figure. The coefficient of friction between the block and cart is μ. The minimum acceleration of the cart so that the block m does not fall is: (a) g/μ (b) μ/g (c) μg (d) Mμg/m

A 10 kg block is placed on an inclined plane with an inclination of 45°. The coefficient of friction between the block and the plane is 0.3. What is the minimum force parallel to the plane required to keep the block at rest? (Take g = 10 m/s²) (a) 50 N (b) 60 N (c) 80 N (d) 100 N

A heavy uniform chain lies on a horizontal table top. If the coefficient of friction between the chain and the table surface is 0.25, then the maximum fraction of the length of the chain that can hang over on edge of the table is : (A) 20% (B) 25% (C) 35% (D) 15%

What is the maximum value of the force F such that the block shown in the arrangement, does not move? (m = √3 kg, μ = 1/(2√3), F at 60° to the horizontal pushing the block down and forward; take g = 10 m/s²) (a) 20 N (b) 10 N (c) 12 N (d) 15 N
Find the distance travelled by the block if μ_K = V₀t/2 and initial velocity of block is V₀? (a) infinite (b) 4V₀/(3√g) (c) V₀²/g (d) 2V₀/g

Minimum force required to keep a block of mass 10 kg at rest against a rough vertical wall (μ = 0.5) is F₀. If a force F₀/2 is applied then find the acceleration of the block in m/s². (Take g = 10 m/s²; same μ for static and kinetic friction)

answer: D a_A becomes constant (horizontal); a_B rises more steeply
stem: A block B is placed on block A. The mass of block B is less than the mass of block A. Friction exists between the blocks, whereas the ground on which the block A is placed is taken to be smooth. A horizontal force F, increasing linearly with time, begins to act on B. The accelerations a_A and a_B of blocks A and B respectively are plotted against t. The correctly plotted graph is (a)–(d): the four a–t graphs shown in the figure
book_key: D a A becomes constant (horizontal); a B rises more steeply

stem: Block B of mass 100 kg rests on a rough surface of friction coefficient μ = 1/3. A rope is tied to block B as shown in figure. The maximum acceleration with which boy A of 25 kg can climb on rope without making block move is : (a) 4g/3 (b) g/3 (c) g/2 (d) 3g/4

Block A of mass m and block B of mass 2m are placed on a fixed triangular wedge by means of a massless, inextensible string and a frictionless pulley as shown. The wedge is inclined at 45° to the horizontal on both sides. The coefficient of friction between block A and the wedge is 2/3 and that between block B and the wedge is 1/3. If the blocks A and B are released from rest, the acceleration of A is ____.

A block rests on a rough inclined plane making an angle of 30° with the horizontal. The coefficient of static friction between the block and the plane is 0.8. If the frictional force on the block is 10 N, the mass of the block (in kg) is (take g = 10 m/s 2 ) (A) 2.0 (B) 4.0 (C) 1.6 (D) 2.5

Two blocks A and B of masses 6 kg and 3 kg rest on a smooth horizontal surface as shown in the figure. If coefficient of friction between A and B is 0.4, the maximum horizontal force which can make them move without separation is (a) 72 N (b) 40 N (c) 36 N (d) 20 N

A block of mass 1 kg is placed over a plank of mass 2 kg. The length of the plank is 2 m. Coefficient of friction between the block and the plank is 0.5 and the ground over which plank is frictionless. A constant force F = 30 N is applied on the plank in horizontal direction. The time after which the block will separate from the plank is (g = 10 m/s²) (a) 0.73 s (b) 1.2 s (c) 0.62 s (d) 1.6 s
